topics.name: Creative studios
topics.definition: Studios whose work is visual and physical, where the site has to show scale and craft rather than describe it.

topics.name: Service businesses
topics.definition: Firms that sell expertise, like law, finance or consulting, where trust and clear answers do the selling.

topics.name: Mission-led teams
topics.definition: Nonprofits and companies doing good, who need a site that explains the mission and is easy for a small team to keep up.

topics.name: Agencies + partners
topics.definition: Studios and agencies that bring me in for the interactive, 3D or CMS-heavy part of a bigger project.

topics.name: Webflow CMS
topics.definition: Collections, fields and templates shaped around how a team publishes, so pages build themselves from content.

topics.name: Interactive 3D
topics.definition: Globes, maps and scenes visitors can turn, zoom and use to decide, fed by the CMS instead of hard-coded.

topics.name: Motion + scroll
topics.definition: Scroll systems, reveals and drag physics built with GSAP and Lenis, with easing tuned by hand.

topics.name: Brand identity
topics.definition: A mark, color and type built on a grid, so the brand holds up from a favicon to a billboard.

topics.name: Design systems
topics.definition: Variables, components and type scales defined once, so page ten is as sharp as page one.

topics.name: Discovery
topics.definition: The first conversation: goals, audience and what a win looks like, before anyone opens Figma.

topics.name: Prototyping
topics.definition: The key pieces built as a clickable prototype and reviewed together before the real build starts.

topics.name: Custom code
topics.definition: Plain JavaScript for what Webflow can't do natively, kept in a repo instead of pasted into settings.

topics.name: Versioned deploys
topics.definition: Every release tagged in GitHub and loaded from jsDelivr with an integrity hash, so any change can be rolled back.

topics.name: Handoff
topics.definition: A walkthrough and a written guide, so the team owns the site, the files and the code after launch.

topics.name: Mobile performance
topics.definition: Heavy visuals that still load fast on a phone: lazy loading, paused loops and a Lighthouse pass on every page.

topics.name: Tap vs hover
topics.definition: A tap fires hover events too. Interactive pieces have to tell a finger from a mouse or they break on phones.

topics.name: Reduced motion
topics.definition: Respecting the system setting that asks for less movement, without turning the site into a static page.

topics.name: Crawlable links
topics.definition: Every page you want found needs a real link in the HTML. Script-only navigation is invisible to search and AI tools.

topics.name: Scope creep
topics.definition: The slow drift of a project past its goal. Named early, it becomes a decision instead of a surprise.

topics.name: Perceived speed
topics.definition: How fast a site feels, which is not always how fast it is. Loading states and motion change the clock in your head.

topics.name: Philosophy at work
topics.definition: Old questions about purpose and meaning, used as working tools for building websites.

topics.name: Science of time
topics.definition: Physics and psychology of time, and what they say about waiting on a screen.

topics.name: Asking better questions
topics.definition: The habit of asking why before how, so the brief describes the problem and not just the wish list.

topics.name: Saying no
topics.definition: Turning down a good idea so the great one ships. The kindest thing a project can hear, early.

topics.name: Search + AI answers
topics.definition: Structured data, clear answers and connected pages, so search engines and AI assistants can tell what a site knows.

topics.name: Knowledge System
topics.definition: A connected content system: a shared vocabulary, a library of answers and pages that link themselves when you tag an entry.

topics.name: Micro-interaction
topics.definition: The small responses to a cursor, a tap or a scroll that make a site feel made by a person.
